title: Calculate a stock's expected move: formula and straddle shortcut
summary: Expected move helps you pick strikes. Formula: stock price x implied volatility x square root of time. For a one-month Apple option near $310 this gives about plus or minus $25.6, so about 68% of the time the price ends between about $284.5 and $335.5. Shortcut: add the at-the-money call and put prices, then multiply by about 1.25 to get one standard deviation.

params.label: Excess drift over rate
params.help: Your view of annual return above the risk-free rate. Zero = the market view; EV is then about zero.

steps.caption: Apple trades near $310. We look one month ahead.
Implied volatility of about 29% turns into a distribution of prices. It widens as time grows.
One standard deviation: $310 x 0.29 x square root of 1/12 is about $25.6. Range about $284.5 to $335.5, 68% of the time.
Two standard deviations cover about 95% of outcomes under the model.
Shortcut: the at-the-money straddle price x 1.25 is about one standard deviation, from Black-Scholes.

takeaways: Expected move = stock price x implied volatility x square root of time in years.
One standard deviation covers about 68% of outcomes under the model.
Shortcut: add the at-the-money call and put, then multiply by about 1.25.
Use the expected move to choose strikes.
caveats: The Apple price and volatility input are partly garbled in the transcript; $310 and 29% match the stated $25.6 move.
Real price moves have fatter tails than the normal model.
